name: Bananaboard
tagline: A lightweight kanban board app for tracking work in columns instead of in your head.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A board with columns, cards, drag and drop and local persistence is one of the most solved problems in software, and an agent will hand you a working one in an afternoon. What it will not hand you is the part that makes a board tool worth paying for: two or more people looking at the same board at the same time without stepping on each other. Realtime sync, conflict handling, invites, permissions and a phone that works offline are each their own weekend, and they compound. If you are the only user, the DIY version is genuinely fine and arguably better because you can bend the schema to your workflow. If anyone else touches the board, you are rebuilding a sync engine for the pleasure of not paying for one.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app with named columns, draggable cards with markdown descriptions and labels, and a SQLite file that survives restarts.
requirements: somewhere to run it: laptop, homelab box or a cheap VPS
a reverse proxy plus basic auth if you want it reachable from your phone
whatYouLose: Realtime multiplayer editing and presence, which is the actual hard part
Native mobile apps and offline sync on a phone
Hosted backups, uptime and someone else waking up when the disk fills
Integrations: Slack, GitHub, calendar, email-in, webhooks
The small polish layer: keyboard shortcuts, undo, search, drag animations that feel right
moatNotes: For solo use there is close to no moat here. The moat appears the moment a second person needs to see the same card move.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a board is a shared artifact, and shared artifacts need a neutral, always-on place to live. People pay so the board is the same board for everyone, loads on a phone in a standup, does not lose a card when two people drag it at once, and does not require anyone on the team to care about where it is hosted. Also because kanban tools are cheap enough that building one is a hobby decision, not a budget decision.
notes: Solo kanban is a Saturday project; team kanban is a sync engine wearing a Saturday project as a hat.
prompt:
Build a single-user kanban board web app that runs entirely on my machine. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript for the frontend
- Express (TypeScript) for the API, same repo, run both with one npm script via concurrently
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/board.db, schema created on first boot
- @dnd-kit/core for drag and drop
- Plain CSS, no UI framework

Data model:
- boards: id, name, created_at
- columns: id, board_id, name, position
- cards: id, column_id, title, body (markdown text), labels (JSON array of strings), position, created_at, updated_at

Features in scope:
- One board seeded with columns: Inbox, Doing, Blocked, Done
- Create, rename, reorder and delete columns
- Create cards inline at the top of a column; click a card to open a side panel with title, markdown body and labels
- Drag cards within and between columns; persist new position via a fractional or integer reindex, do not lose ordering on reload
- Filter cards by text and by label from a single search input
- Archive instead of hard delete for cards; an Archive view to restore or purge
- Keyboard: n for new card in the focused column, / to focus search, Escape to close the panel
- GET /api/export returns the whole board as JSON; POST /api/import replaces it from the same shape

Out of scope, do not build: auth, multi-user, realtime websockets, invites, notifications, third-party integrations, mobile apps, analytics.

Rules:
- Any config goes in .env, read with process.env, and ship a .env.example. No secrets committed.
- Optimistic UI updates with rollback on API error.
- Include a README with setup, run and backup instructions (backup is: copy data/board.db).
- Add a seed script that inserts about 20 sample cards so the UI is not empty on first run.
- Verify it runs with npm install && npm run dev before you tell me you are done.
